name: Dispersion Trade (Short Index Vol vs Long Single-Name Vol)
summary: Sell index volatility and buy volatility on the index's largest constituents, betting that realized correlation falls short of the correlation implied by the spread between index and single-name option prices.

legs.strike_rule: index leg, defined-risk wrapper: short SPY strangle or iron condor at 0.15-0.20 delta per side (the short index vol)
index leg, the matching put side of the same wrapper, each short covered by a long wing
single-name leg: long strangles on 5-10 of the largest index constituents, delta 0.25-0.35, vega-weighted to the index short
legs.dte_rule: same expiry as the index leg

legs.strike_rule: single-name leg: the matching long puts, same names and expiry

max_profit: Unbounded in principle - realized dispersion accrues as the single-name gammas pay more than the index gamma costs
max_loss: Bounded by construction only if the index short is wrapped in wings: index-side defined loss plus the entire single-name debit. In its pure (naked index strangle) form the loss is UNDEFINED.
breakevens: Not expressible as a price level - the trade breaks even when realized index vol squared equals the weighted sum of realized single-name vols squared times the entry implied correlation

greeks.delta: targeted to zero across the book and rehedged daily
greeks.gamma: positive in the names, negative in the index - the entire P/L is the difference
greeks.theta: negative overall; the single-name premium usually costs more than the index premium collected
greeks.vega: roughly flat by construction, which is the point

when_to_use: When implied correlation (derivable from index IV versus the cap-weighted single-name IVs) sits in the top decile of its two-year range - typically right after an index-level shock, when index puts are bid and single names are not. It is the canonical volatility-surface trade and has no representative anywhere else in the bank.
entry_rules: CAPITAL GATE - READ FIRST: a minimally diversified dispersion book needs 5-10 single-name strangles plus a wrapped index position. At realistic option prices that is $15k-$30k of premium and 12-24 legs. On a $50k account this is not runnable at meaningful size; document it, and require explicit authorization before any live version.
Index short MUST be wrapped (iron condor, not naked strangle) to stay inside level 3 - every short leg needs a long leg of the same right and expiry.
Implied correlation at entry >= its 80th percentile over 2 years, computed from SPY IV and the cap-weighted IVs of the top 10 holdings.
Single-name basket: 5-10 names, each >= 2% of index weight, each with OI >= 250 at the chosen strikes, none with earnings inside the expiry.
Vega-weight the basket to 1.0-1.3x the index short's vega; below 1.0 the trade is just short vol with extra steps.
Total defined risk (index wing loss + single-name debit) <= 6% of equity.
management_rules: Delta-hedge the whole book daily to within +/-0.10 net delta per $10k of notional, using shares of the index or the names.
Take profit when implied correlation falls below its 50th percentile, or at 40% of maximum modeled gain.
Cut the entire book if implied correlation rises 10 percentile points above entry - the thesis is measurably wrong.
Replace any single name that announces a merger or is added to an acquisition rumor list; deal-driven names stop behaving like index constituents.
Roll the whole book together at 21 DTE, never leg by leg.
exit_rules: Flatten all index short legs by 15:45 ET on expiration day; flatten the single-name shorts (if any wrapper shorts exist) at the same time.
Close any short leg at extrinsic < $0.10 or |delta| >= 0.85, and short calls before every ex-dividend date while ITM - with 5-10 names this is a daily calendar check, not an occasional one.
Close long single-name legs rather than exercising them; an exercised long call buys 100 shares of a single name.
If any single-name leg becomes unquotable (no two-sided market for a full session), close the entire book - the hedge ratios are no longer measurable.
assignment_risk: Multiplied by the number of names. Every wrapper short on the index and every short in a name is separately assignable, and the single-name legs carry their own ex-dividend calendars. An account that must never be assigned should treat this structure as a research object rather than a position.
buying_power: Index condor width x 100 per unit, plus the full single-name debit, plus daily hedging cash.
liquidity_needs: The most demanding in the bank: SPY plus 5-10 mega-cap chains, all needing tight two-sided markets at roll time.
common_mistakes: Running it naked on the index side; equal-weighting the basket instead of vega-weighting; ignoring the daily delta hedge, which is where dispersion P/L is actually realized; sizing it as if the single-name debit were the only cost.
zero_dte_notes: Not applicable - correlation is realized over weeks, not hours.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
